newsitem.title: CANADA: Saudi barley tender seen next week - Canada trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi barley tender seen next week - Canada trade.

text.p: Saudi Arabia was expected to tender for barley next week after stepping out of the market in the past week, Canadian grain trade sources said Thursday.
"Their budget did go through on the 24th (December 24) but it's just a question of waiting until Europe gets back to work," one cash-connected trade source here said.
European traders said last week they expected Saudi Arabia to be seeking about 500,000 tonnes of barley this week.
"Europe doesn't really get back to work until Monday, so there's no point in putting a tender out if you're not going to have all the parties playing," the Canadian cash source added.
Saudi Arabia normally buys about 40 percent of the world's feed barley exports.

On December 19 the Canadian Wheat Board held its latest world feed barley price forecast firm at C$140-C$160 a tonne on expectations the Saudis may buy as much as 50 percent of supplies in the current 1996/97 (Aug/July) crop year, or about five million tonnes.
